item.title: Dangerously overgrown grass around recreational area, 28th July
item.description:
I live on the Greyhound Estate in Longlevens. There is a green area for public recreation use sited between Greyhound Gardens and Blackwater Way. There is 2/3rds f this area which is regularly cut by Council employees and used by many local residents - no problem, thank you. However, the remaining 1/3 of this green area sited at the actual junction of Greyhound Gardens and Blackwater Way which has been let unattended by Council employees for some considerable time - 2 r 3 years. It is now a disgraceful, unuseable site. This unattended area was an offroad gateway to the whole green and was used by Caravan Dwellers to set up site in the year of August 2019. To prevent further use, trees were planted which have now grown to a size that prevents such a re-occurence. Additionally, contractor have attended and sited posts around the public footpath bordering the green which has added to access security. I now bring your attention to this eyesore on the estate. All other green areas are Council tended so why no this area? The grass is 2ft in places between the trees and in other places, brambles are prevalent. I ask that Council employees attend the site and strim the grass between the trees plus cut back the bramble bushes to allow residents to walk among the trees and enjoy recreation in the full area of this grassed area. Many thanks,

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Blackwater Way, Elmbridge, Gloucester
Report on FixMyStreet
